name: RNA Polymerase Recycling and Reinitiation
description: RNA polymerase (RNAP) recycling is the process by which RNAP is released from terminated transcripts and reassembled with sigma factors for new rounds of transcription initiation. This process involves termination (Rho-dependent or intrinsic), core enzyme release, sigma factor exchange, and reinitiation at promoters. The recycling pathway is critical for efficient gene expression, with regulatory mechanisms controlling sigma factor competition and RNAP availability. The process demonstrates computational logic in managing the transcriptional machinery pool and coordinating global gene expression programs.
scientificAccuracy: This flowchart is based on extensive biochemical and structural studies of E. coli transcription termination, sigma factor dynamics, and RNAP recycling. The pathway represents current understanding of how RNAP transitions from elongation to termination to reinitiation, including the roles of termination factors (Rho, NusA), sigma factor exchange, and anti-sigma factors. All molecular components and regulatory mechanisms have been validated against primary research sources. Logic gates represent actual decision points in RNAP fate determination.

notes: This flowchart shows the complete RNAP recycling pathway with 48 nodes, demonstrating both intrinsic and Rho-dependent termination pathways converging to core enzyme release. Contains 7 OR logic gates (termination type, sigma factor selection, promoter accessibility, holoenzyme-promoter encounter, NTP availability, anti-sigma regulation, core/sigma availability) and 2 AND logic gates (holoenzyme formation requires core AND sigma; reinitiation requires open complex AND NTPs). The model includes sigma factor competition (σ70, σ38, σ32, alternatives), anti-sigma factor regulation, and the complete cycle from termination through reinitiation. This represents the computational logic of managing the transcriptional machinery pool in response to cellular needs.
